title: Types and variable declarations
summary: Variables have static types; var infers a local type from its initializer.
rules: var requires an initializer and does not mean dynamic.
Use decimal for base-ten financial arithmetic; use invariant formatting for machine output.

title: Nullable types and operators
summary: Nullable value types and annotated reference types make absence explicit.
rules: Nullable reference analysis is enabled in the playground.
The null-forgiving operator ! suppresses a warning; it does not check a value at runtime.

title: Control flow
summary: Branches select work; loops repeat it over values or conditions.
rules: Conditions must be bool.
continue skips the current iteration; break exits the nearest loop.

title: Method
summary: Methods declare parameter and return types and may be expression-bodied.
syntax:
ReturnType Method(Type parameter) { return expression; }
static int Double(int value) => value * 2;
rules: Validate preconditions before work.
Overloads differ by parameter signatures, not just return type.

title: Class
summary: Classes combine state, constructors, properties and behavior.
rules: Classes have reference semantics.
Restrict setters to preserve invariants.

title: Interface
summary: Interfaces declare contracts that different implementations can satisfy.
syntax:
interface IContract { string Describe(); }
class Item : IContract { public string Describe() => "item"; }
rules: Implement interface members publicly or explicitly.
Depend on a small contract rather than a concrete implementation when variation is useful.

title: Record
summary: Records provide value equality and convenient nondestructive copies.
syntax:
public record Item(string Name, int Quantity);
var changed = item with { Quantity = 2 };
rules: A record class remains a reference type; record struct is a value type.
Value equality does not make nested mutable objects immutable.

title: Generics
summary: Type parameters let algorithms preserve caller types.
syntax:
static T Choose<T>(IEnumerable<T> values) { /* return a T */ }
class Store<T> where T : notnull { }
rules: Constraints describe required capabilities.
Document empty-sequence behavior rather than using a misleading default(T).

title: Collections
summary: Generic collections store typed sequences, sets and key/value entries.
rules: TryGetValue handles missing keys without exceptions.
Choose an explicit comparer when string key equality matters.

title: Pattern matching
summary: Patterns test shape or value and can bind typed locals.
syntax:
var result = value switch { null => fallback, Type item => Use(item), _ => other };
if (value is Type item) { Use(item); }
rules: Switch expressions need an exhaustive result.
Pattern matching handles null explicitly without dereferencing it.

title: Linq group
summary: LINQ composes typed filters, projections and aggregations over sequences.
syntax:
var result = source.Where(item => predicate).Select(item => value).ToArray();
var groups = source.GroupBy(item => item.Key);
rules: Many operators execute lazily; materialize when a snapshot is needed.
Order results explicitly when consumers need deterministic order.

title: Exception
summary: Exceptions report exceptional failure; catch only failures you can handle.
syntax:
try { Work(); } catch (SpecificException error) { Recover(error); } finally { Cleanup(); }
throw new ArgumentException("message");
rules: Use throw; to rethrow without resetting the stack trace.
Prefer TryParse for ordinary invalid user input.

title: Async cancellation
summary: Task-returning methods expose completion and errors; cancellation is cooperative.
rules: Pass the token through every cancellable operation.
Await tasks to observe errors; avoid async void except event handlers.

title: Dispose resource
summary: using statements and declarations dispose owned synchronous resources on every exit path.
syntax:
using (var resource = Create()) { Use(resource); }
using var resource = Create();
rules: A using declaration disposes at the end of its enclosing scope.
The owner disposes a resource; do not dispose borrowed resources unexpectedly.

title: Async dispose
summary: await using awaits an asynchronous disposal operation before leaving scope.
syntax:
await using var resource = CreateAsyncDisposable();
await resource.WorkAsync(token);
rules: Implement IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync returning ValueTask.
Dispose even when the body fails; avoid disposing a resource before outstanding operations finish.

title: File io
summary: System.IO provides path composition and file operations, including cancellable async methods.
rules: Use temporary paths in tests.
Do not build paths by concatenating separators; propagate I/O errors appropriately.

title: Json deserialize
summary: System.Text.Json maps JSON to typed objects but domain validation remains explicit.
rules: Catch JsonException for malformed JSON or incompatible JSON types.
Check null and semantic constraints after deserialization; nullable annotations alone do not validate external data.

title: Http client
summary: HttpClient sends cancellable requests; a response status is separate from transport failure.
rules: Reuse HttpClient or use IHttpClientFactory; dispose each response.
Cancellation throws OperationCanceledException; non-success status is checked explicitly.

title: Minimal API routing
summary: ASP.NET Core minimal APIs map route handlers directly and serialize typed results.
rules: Use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web for the hosting application.
The Web SDK supplies ASP.NET Core; no controller package is needed.

title: Minimal api validation
summary: Explicit validation gives a minimal endpoint a predictable public error contract.
rules: These examples validate explicitly and do not require the optional .NET 10 validation package.
Malformed JSON is rejected by ASP.NET Core binding before the handler.

title: Api error responses
summary: HTTP error results communicate expected failures without exposing private exception details.
syntax:
return Results.Problem(title: "Unavailable", statusCode: 503);
return Results.Conflict(new { error = "already_exists" });
rules: Use consistent status codes and machine-readable fields.
Do not return stack traces or exception messages to public clients.

title: Api request tests
summary: WebApplicationFactory hosts the real application with TestServer for local HTTP tests.
rules: Tests reference the web project and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing 10.0.13.
Expose the generated entry point with public partial class Program; tests use no listening port.

title: Xunit fact
summary: xUnit discovers public test methods marked Fact.
syntax:
[Fact]
public void Behavior() { Assert.Equal(expected, actual); }
rules: Pin xunit and its test adapter in the test project.
Assert observable behavior; avoid depending on test execution order.

title: Data-driven theories
summary: A Theory executes once per supplied data row.
rules: InlineData supports attribute-compatible constants.
Use separate rows for boundaries and representative interior values.

title: Xunit async assertions
summary: Task-returning tests await operations and asynchronous exception assertions.
syntax:
[Fact]
public async Task Failure() { await Assert.ThrowsAsync<ExpectedException>(() => WorkAsync()); }
rules: Await the assertion itself so a failure cannot escape the test.
ThrowsAsync checks the exact type; ThrowsAnyAsync accepts derived exceptions.
